docs.title: 🛡️ SATGuardian Edge WAF (satguardian)
docs.text:
Status: research prototype, not a production-ready WAF. Detection has only been measured on a small, hand-written, in-sample corpus. The Python comparison harness runs local stand-ins, not real Coraza, SafeLine or ModSecurity. See STATUS.md and corpus/README.md for the evidence and its limits.

📚 Official Documentation: https://exactorresearch.github.io/satguardian/

SATGuardian Edge WAF is an experimental, self-hosted Web Application Firewall written in Rust. It evaluates security logic with 128-bit integer bitmasks (u128) in microseconds on the edge, backed by out-of-band EXACTOR GXOR boolean cloud optimization. Detection quality is measured, not assumed: the numbers below come from a versioned corpus and a reproducible benchmark, and they are explicitly in-sample.

docs.title: 1. Awareness: The Problem with Traditional WAFs
docs.text:
Modern API gateways, microservices, and web applications face an impossible security trade-off:

                  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │ THE TRADITIONAL WAF DILEMMA             │
                  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                       │
        ┌──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┐
        ▼                                                             ▼
┌──────────────────────────────┐                            ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│  Regex & Anomaly Scoring     │                            │  Probabilistic "AI/ML" WAFs  │
│  (ModSecurity / Coraza CRS)  │                            │  (NLP / Token Weights)       │
├──────────────────────────────┤                            ├──────────────────────────────┤
│ ❌ Heavy CPU Overhead        │                            │ ❌ High False Positive Rates │
│    (rule-set dependent)      │                            │    (Blocks technical prose)  │
│ ❌ Evasion Vulnerability     │                            │ ❌ Unpredictable Box Black   │
│    (Triple URL / Comment)    │                            │    (Zero auditability)       │
└──────────────────────────────┘                            └──────────────────────────────┘
  1. The Latency Tax of Rule Sets: Evaluating many regular expressions across multiple HTTP targets (URI, headers, body) adds CPU work to every request. How much depends on the rule set, paranoia level and hardware; this repository does not benchmark the real OWASP CRS, so no vendor latency number is claimed.
  2. Evasion via Obfuscation: Single-pass regex engines can miss nested encodings (..%25252f), inline comments (UNION/**/SELECT) and DOM event mutations. The local unnormalized-regex stand-in misses 47.0% of attacks on the in-repo stream; that figure describes the stand-in, not ModSecurity.
  3. The False Positive Problem: Token-weight classifiers can flag technical prose such as "script", "select" or "character". The local heuristic stand-in blocks 24.6% of benign controls on the in-repo stream; it is not a trained model and does not represent a commercial classifier.

docs.text:
SATGuardian resolves this dilemma by decoupling in-path edge inspection from out-of-band boolean rule synthesis.

│                                                                            │
│  HTTP Request ──► Multi-Pass Lexer ──► 128-Bit FeatureVector (u128)        │
│                   (src/ast/lexer.rs)   (src/ast/features.rs)               │
│                                                 │                          │
│                                                 ▼                          │
│                                 Bitwise Rule Mask Evaluation               │
│                                 (minterm & mask) == expected               │
│                                 (~20 µs p50 in-memory, native Rust)        │
│                                        /               \                   │
│                                   [ALLOW]             [BLOCK + Causal Log] │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────┘

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. CONTROL PLANE: OFFLINE ADVISOR & CLOUD SYNTHESIS (Security Units - SU) │
│                                                                            │
│  waf_ledger.db ──► EXACTOR GXOR (AND, OR, NOT, XOR)    ──► Digital Twin    │
│  (3,799 logs)      128-Variable Boolean Minimization       Replay (FP gate) │
│                    (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs)             │         │
│                                                                  ▼         │
│                                                   Atomic ArcSwap Hot-Reload│
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 2.1 Native Rust In-Path Edge Engine (src/)
docs.text:
• Multi-Pass Lexical Normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs): Applies percent-decoding, unwraps MySQL executable comments, strips inline comments, decodes HTML entities and Unicode/overlong escapes, and expands Log4j lookups before token extraction. Entity-encoded payloads are covered by corpus/independent_v1.json; that is a regression check, not proof of complete coverage.
  • 128-Bit Feature Vector (src/ast/features.rs): Packs HTTP attributes, Shannon character entropy, and structural tokens across 5 domains (SQLi, XSS, RCE, LFI, SSRF) into a single u128 integer.
  • Bitmask Conjunction Evaluation (src/engine/sat_solver.rs): Compares request minterms against compiled rule masks via bitwise AND operations ((minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits). On the pinned corpus at 10,000 requests the native engine measured roughly 20 µs p50 and 22–25 µs mean in-memory; p99 is load dependent and has measured 50–60 µs.
  • Structural token conjunctions: Rules require combinations such as TAG_OPEN \(\land\) SCRIPT_ELEMENT \(\land\) DOM_EXEC instead of single keywords. False positives are counted on the pinned corpus; the engine does not claim zero FPs.

docs.title: 2.2 Out-of-Band Cloud Synthesis: EXACTOR GXOR (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs)
docs.text: When novel attack patterns are recorded in waf_ledger.db, SATGuardian sends the 128-bit minterms to the EXACTOR GXOR cloud optimization engine: * Linear \(O(\text{term\_count})\) Scaling: Uses Differential Gray Code Mapping (modify_gray_code) to locate logical neighbors in \(O(1)\) constant time, avoiding the \(O(2^n)\) exponential blow-up of classical Quine-McCluskey / Espresso minimizers. * Full Operator Basis {AND, OR, NOT, XOR}: Minimizes parity, equivalence, and symmetric security predicates across up to 128 variables (u128). The size reduction versus a naive Sum-of-Products expansion is not measured in this repository. * Digital Twin Replay: Replays candidate rules against recorded benign traffic (satguardian-advisor.py), reports collisions, and requires human approval before hot-reloading via lock-free ArcSwap.

docs.title: 3.3 100% On-Premise Traffic Sovereignty
docs.text:
SATGuardian runs entirely inside your infrastructure. We never host customer traffic or require DNS CNAME redirects:

  1. Kubernetes / Envoy Proxy Native Sidecar: Runs alongside Envoy via ext_authz over an in-memory Unix Domain Socket (unix:///run/satguardian/waf.sock), adding the engine's measured per-request latency (tens of microseconds) with no network hop.
  2. Reverse Proxy: Frontline protection for Nginx, Apache, or Microsoft IIS (including Windows Service deployment via install.ps1).
  3. Standalone Binary: Zero-dependency, self-contained Rust binary (satguardian-waf proxy --listen 127.0.0.1:8080). It speaks plain HTTP; terminate TLS in a reverse proxy or Envoy in front of it.

docs.title: 4. Action: Getting Started in 4 Easy Steps
docs.text: Follow this step-by-step onboarding journey to evaluate SATGuardian in your environment:

docs.title: Step 1: Download & Run the Standalone Binary Benchmark (30 Seconds)
docs.text:
Test the self-contained standalone binary directly on your machine across 10,000 HTTP requests with zero dependencies:

# Using pre-compiled standalone binary
.\satguardian-waf.exe benchmark -r 10000

# Or building directly from source via cargo
cargo run --release -- benchmark -r 10000

docs.title: Step 2: Run the Multi-WAF Comparative Benchmark
docs.text:
Run the Python reference harness against the local stand-ins:

python run_benchmark.py 1000

This does not execute Coraza, SafeLine, ModSecurity or an LLM. It compares the Python SATGuardian port with small Python reimplementations on the in-repo payload list. The report prints the provenance and the caveat.

docs.title: Step 3: Deploy in Staging / Local Envoy Sidecar
docs.text:
Launch the standalone reverse proxy or attach SATGuardian to your Envoy proxy via ext_authz:

# Standalone reverse proxy. It speaks plain HTTP: terminate TLS in front of it.
# The management API is isolated on 127.0.0.1:10001 and requires a bearer token.
export SATGUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
satguardian-waf proxy --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 --upstream http://127.0.0.1:3000

# Daily example: inspect metrics from the local management listener
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SATGUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  http://127.0.0.1:10001/api/waf/metrics

Security defaults introduced in this release:

  • Management routes (/api/waf/*) return 503 until SATGUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN (or WAF_ADMIN_TOKEN) is set.
  • The management API listens only on 127.0.0.1:10001; set WAF_ADMIN_LISTEN_ADDR to change it or off to disable it.
  • Inbound bodies are capped at 2 MiB (WAF_MAX_BODY_BYTES); larger requests get 413.
  • Forwarding headers are ignored unless the TCP peer is in WAF_TRUSTED_PROXIES (loopback is always trusted).
  • Blocked responses are generic by default. Use --verbose only in development.
  • Upstream responses are streamed, so SSE and large downloads are no longer buffered. WebSocket upgrades are not supported yet.

docs.title: Detection corpus and measurement protocol
docs.text: This directory contains hand-labelled HTTP requests used by tests/independent_corpus_test.rs. The corpus is small and hand-written on purpose: it exists to make regressions visible, not to certify real-world accuracy.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
File Contents Status independent_v1.json 63 attacks + 16 benign controls across SQLi, XSS, RCE, LFI, SSRF, GraphQL, prototype pollution, JWT, framework exploits, WordPress and file exposure. Regression suite after the 2026-11-01 fix pass. heldout_v1.json 17 attack variants + 4 benign controls written after the first fix pass. Measured once before correction, then kept as a regression suite.

Payload provenance is recorded per case in the note field and in the provenance block: OWASP CRS/WSTG notes, PortSwigger filter-evasion notes, Log4Shell obfuscation catalogues, RFC 7519 JWT fixtures, and benign snippets modelled on framework/CDN documentation.

docs.title: Regression run after fixes
docs.text: Both files currently report 100% recall and 0% false-positive rate in cargo test --test independent_corpus_test. These are in-sample regression numbers. Every case was used to drive the fixes above, so they say "the pinned cases still pass", not "the engine catches X% of real attacks". No held-out estimate exists after the second fix pass because the held-out set was consumed.

docs.title: Rules for changing the corpus
docs.text:
1. Label a case before running it against the engine. Do not add a case and then label it from the engine output.
  2. Keep the note and provenance. A case without a source is not reviewable.
  3. When a case fails, fix the engine or document the gap. Do not delete the case to make the suite green.
  4. If you consume a held-out batch by tuning against it, say so here and create a new batch instead of reusing the old label.
  5. Do not publish corpus metrics as independent quality evidence. The docs/ benchmark pages must link to this file and repeat the caveat.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
cargo test --test independent_corpus_test -- --nocapture

The test prints per-category recall, every miss, every false positive, and every category-attribution mismatch, then fails if any list is non-empty or if recall/FPR cross the regression thresholds.

docs.title: What is not measured
docs.text:
• No independent or third-party evaluation. The corpus is hand-written in this repository. There is no held-out estimate after the second fix pass.
  • No comparison against real WAF products. The Python harness (run_benchmark.py) runs local stand-ins written for this repository. Rows named Coraza, SafeLine, ModSecurity or "probabilistic NLP" are reimplementations, not those products. They must never be cited as vendor benchmarks.
  • No production soak. No staged rollout, no traffic replay at scale, no long-running memory or rule-update testing.
  • No TLS or WebSocket handling in the standalone proxy. TLS terminates in front of it; WebSocket upgrades are rejected.
  • No ESP32/embedded port. Embedded deployment is a research direction only.
  • Prebuilt artifacts under dist/ and releases/ are stale. They were built before the claims were corrected and still contain the old banner text. Rebuild or delete them before publishing; do not ship them as current.

docs.title: Why this file exists
docs.text:
Earlier versions of this repository published a benchmark that:

  • capped perfect accuracy at 99.9% and floored zero error rates at 0.1%;
  • labelled Python regex stand-ins as "Coraza WAF (OWASP CRS v4)" and "SafeLine WAF (Chaitin T1K)";
  • derived "3.38x faster", "15.0x faster" and "reduced false negatives by N percentage points" headlines from those stand-ins;
  • presented the numbers as production evidence.

Those claims were fabricated or misleading. The cap/floor logic is gone, the stand-ins are labelled, and the Rust benchmark now refuses to run without the versioned corpus. The guardrail tests in tests/docs_claims_test.rs fail the build if the banned claims or unlabelled comparisons return.

Treat a green test suite as "no known regressions on pinned inputs", not as "safe for production".

docs.title: Structured Grammar Inspection & Offline Rule Synthesis
docs.text:
Architectural Overview: In-Path Bitmask Evaluation and Out-of-Band EXACTOR GXOR ({AND, OR, NOT, XOR}) Minimization up to 128 Variables Codebase Reference: src/engine/sat_solver.rs, src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, exactor-core-v128, satguardian-advisor.py

Status: research prototype. Detection numbers in this document are in-sample results on a hand-written corpus and comparisons against local Python stand-ins. They are not vendor benchmarks and do not establish production readiness. See STATUS.md.

docs.title: 1. Core Engineering Problem
docs.text:
Enterprise Web Application Firewalls face an operational trade-off between latency, evasion resilience, and false positive rates:

  1. Unnormalized Signature WAFs: fast on simple strings but bypassable by inline comments, URL encoding or alternative DOM vectors. The local unnormalized-regex stand-in misses 47.0% of attacks on the in-repo stream; that is a property of the stand-in, not a measurement of ModSecurity.
  2. Multi-Target Anomaly Scoring WAFs (OWASP CRS / Coraza): broader coverage requires transformation passes and dozens of rule evaluations per request. The local CRS-style stand-in costs 0.2350 ms average in Python and misses 5.4% on the same stream. No claim is made about the real engine, whose rule count, paranoia level and tuning differ substantially.
  3. Probabilistic Token / NLP Classifiers: fixed token weights can fire on legitimate technical prose. The local hand-written heuristic scores a 24.6% false-positive rate on the in-repo benign controls; it is not a trained model.

docs.title: 2.1 Plane 1: In-Path Lexical & Bitmask Engine (src/engine/sat_solver.rs)
docs.text:
• Single-Pass Canonicalization: Decodes nested URL encodings, strips inline comments (/**/), and extracts structural grammar tokens across five domains (ISLAND-SQLI, ISLAND-XSS, ISLAND-RCE, ISLAND-LFI, ISLAND-SSRF).
  • Bitwise Conjunction Evaluation: Evaluates compiled rules via u128 bitwise masks. Rules require structural conjunctions rather than isolated keywords. On the 16 benign controls in corpus/independent_v1.json the engine produced no false positives; that sample is too small to generalize.

docs.title: 2.2 Plane 2: Out-of-Band EXACTOR GXOR Synthesis & Digital Twin (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, exactor-core-v128, satguardian-advisor.py)
docs.text:
• Minterm Harvesting: Novel high-entropy anomalies (14 pending u128 minterms in the current waf_ledger.db) and hostile IP/route patterns are logged asynchronously to SQLite without slowing down the hot path.
  • EXACTOR GXOR Boolean Minimization (Up to 128 Variables): Unlike classical Quine-McCluskey or Espresso algorithms—which are restricted to {AND, OR, NOT} and suffer from \(O(2^n)\) exponential blow-up beyond 20–30 variables—the EXACTOR GXOR engine (procesar_gxor in exactor-core-v128) operates over the complete {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} (\(\{\land, \lor, \neg, \oplus\}\)) basis using Differential Gray Code Mapping (modify_gray_code). By locating logical neighbors via Gray Code lookups and collapsing symmetric/parity patterns into native XOR/NXOR operations, GXOR is designed to scale as \(O(\text{term\_count})\) across all 128 variables (u128). The size reduction versus a naive Sum-of-Products expansion is not measured in this repository.
  • Digital Twin Replay (SimulationAgent): Every candidate rule is replayed against the benign requests recorded in waf_ledger.db. Rules that collide with known-good traffic are rejected. The collision counts depend on the ledger contents and are not a fixed guarantee.

docs.title: 4. Commercial & Operational Continuity Model
docs.text:
1. 100% On-Premise Traffic Sovereignty: The Edge WAF runs entirely inside the customer's infrastructure (Standalone binary, Reverse Proxy in front of Nginx/Apache/IIS, or Kubernetes Envoy Sidecar). Customer traffic is never routed through external DNS CNAME bastions.
  2. Unlimited Edge Inspection at $0.00/Request: In-path request inspection is 100% free and unlimited.
  3. Security Units (SU) for Cloud GXOR Rule Optimization: Cloud-assisted EXACTOR GXOR boolean synthesis is metered in Security Units (SU) based on the number of variables (up to 128 in SaaS tiers) and minterms compressed. If an organization's monthly SU quota is exhausted (HTTP 402 SU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED), cloud optimization pauses while the local Edge WAF continues protecting traffic uninterrupted with its last compiled bitmask matrix.

docs.title: SATGuardian Methodology: Lexical Tokenization, Bitmask Evaluation & Offline Rule Minimization
docs.text:
Technical Architecture Specification Codebase Reference: src/ast/lexer.rs, src/ast/features.rs, src/engine/sat_solver.rs, src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, exactor-core-v128

Status: research prototype. Detection evidence is limited to a small in-sample corpus; see STATUS.md.

docs.title: 1. Architectural Separation: Hot Path vs. Offline Control Plane
docs.text:
A core engineering principle of SATGuardian Edge WAF is the strict separation between in-path request evaluation (which must execute in microseconds with predictable latency) and out-of-band rule optimization (which performs 128-variable algebraic boolean minimization asynchronously via EXACTOR GXOR).

Subsystem Execution Path Implemented Algorithm Computational Complexity Measured Latency Lexical Decoder & Tokenizer In-Path (Edge WAF) Iterative URL/HTML decoding + comment stripping + token scan (src/ast/lexer.rs) \(O(L)\) where \(L\) is payload byte length ~6–10 µs (Rust) Bitmask Rule Evaluator In-Path (Edge WAF) 128-bit FeatureVector bitwise comparison (src/engine/sat_solver.rs) \(O(R)\) bitwise operations (\(R \le 64\) rules) ~4–6 µs (Rust) Total Edge Hot Path In-Path (Edge WAF) Combined Lexer + Bitmask Evaluator Linear in payload size, constant per rule ~20 µs p50 / ~22 µs avg (in-memory) EXACTOR GXOR Boolean Minimizer Out-of-Band (Cloud / Advisor) Differential Gray Code Mapping + {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} reduction (exactor-core-v128) \(O(\text{term\_count})\) linear scaling up to 128 vars 10–250 ms (Background) Digital Twin Verifier Out-of-Band (satguardian-advisor.py) Historical replay over benign SQLite ledger (waf_ledger.db) \(O(N_{\text{benign}})\) ~50 ms for 1,663 benign logs

Important Clarification: SATGuardian does not execute an NP-complete backtracking SAT solver (such as DPLL or CDCL) on the live HTTP request path, nor is it limited by the 20–30 variable exponential ceiling of classical Quine-McCluskey. Out-of-band logic minimization is powered by EXACTOR GXOR, which simplifies up to 128 Boolean variables (u128) over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} and compiles the reduced invariants into u128 bitmasks for single-cycle bitwise evaluation on the edge.

docs.title: 2. Stage 1: Multi-Pass Lexical Normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs)
docs.text:
Attackers frequently evade traditional signature WAFs by nesting encodings (e.g., double or triple URL encoding ..%25252f, HTML entity encoding, or inline SQL comments /**/).

SATGuardian's lexer (Lexer::normalize_and_tokenize) applies a bounded, deterministic normalization pipeline before extracting grammatical tokens: 1. Iterative Percent-Decoding: Unwinds nested URL encodings up to a fixed recursion bound so obfuscated sequences resolve to their canonical ASCII characters. 2. Comment & Whitespace Canonicalization: Strips inline C/SQL comments (/* ... */) and collapses redundant whitespace so UNION/**/ALL/**/SELECT normalizes cleanly. 3. Contextual Token Extraction: Scans the normalized stream to identify structural tokens across five security domains ("Certainty Islands"): - ISLAND-SQLI: Quote delimiters, boolean tautologies ('1'='1', 1=1), UNION SELECT projections, stacked DDL (; DROP TABLE), and time-delay primitives (SLEEP, WAITFOR DELAY, BENCHMARK). - ISLAND-XSS: Executable <script> blocks, inline DOM event handlers (onerror=, onload=), <svg/onload>, and javascript:/data: pseudo-protocols. - ISLAND-RCE: Shell chaining operators (;, |, &&, `, $()) coupled with system binaries (cat, whoami, bash, curl, powershell) or dynamic evaluation sinks (os.system, eval(), subprocess). - ISLAND-LFI: Directory traversal sequences (../, ..\) and direct kernel/system file descriptors (/etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ, win.ini). - ISLAND-SSRF: Internal cloud metadata targets (169.254.169.254), loopback addresses (127.0.0.1, localhost), and non-HTTP proxy schemes (gopher://, dict://, file://).

docs.title: 3. Stage 2: 128-Bit Feature Vector & Bitmask Evaluation (src/ast/features.rs, src/engine/sat_solver.rs)
docs.text:
During inspection, extracted lexical properties and HTTP metadata are packed into a 128-bit integer (FeatureVector(pub u128)):

// Fast O(1) bitwise evaluation of a compiled rule cube against the request minterm
#[inline(always)]
pub fn matches_minterm(minterm: u128, required_mask: u128, expected_bits: u128) -> bool {
    (minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits
}

docs.title: Why SATGuardian Uses Bitmask Conjunctions
docs.text:
1. Structural Context vs. Substring Matching: A benign user comment containing the words "script" and "character" activates isolated keyword flags, which causes the local token-weight stand-in to produce false positives (24.6% on the in-repo stream). In SATGuardian, rule SAT-XSS-01 requires the simultaneous presence of TAG_OPEN \(\land\) SCRIPT_ELEMENT \(\land\) DOM_EXEC; the pinned corpus records no benign collision for it, which is a regression observation and too small a sample to generalize.
  2. Predictable CPU Execution: Bitwise operations on a u128 register execute in a few CPU clock cycles without backtracking, preventing Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).
  3. Human-Auditable Causal Traces: Every blocked request records the exact rule ID, active token set, and boolean clause in waf_ledger.db (e.g., (SELECT_PROJECTION AND UNION_CLAUSE) violates [SAT-SQLI-02] -> ACTION_BLOCK [sql_injection]).

docs.title: 4. Stage 3: Out-of-Band EXACTOR GXOR Boolean Minimization (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, exactor-core-v128)
docs.text:
When the Edge WAF encounters anomalous high-entropy requests or repeated hostile bursts that do not match an existing compiled cube, it logs the observed 128-bit minterm in the novel_anomalies table of waf_ledger.db.

Out of band, SatguardianCloudClient (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs) and the Multi-Agent Advisor (satguardian-advisor.py) invoke the EXACTOR GXOR engine (procesar_gxor in exactor-core-v128) to compress these u128 minterms across up to 128 variables: 1. Differential Gray Code Mapping (modify_gray_code): Rather than performing exhaustive \(O(m^2)\) pairwise comparisons like classical Quine-McCluskey, EXACTOR projects u128 minterms into Gray Code space and locates logical neighbors in \(O(1)\) constant time via BTreeMap/HashMap lookups, achieving \(O(\text{term\_count})\) linear scaling. 2. GXOR / NXOR Algebraic Reduction over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR}: Classical {AND, OR, NOT} minimizers suffer from exponential clause explosion when simplifying symmetric, parity, or cross-dependent security predicates. EXACTOR GXOR detects exclusive-OR (XOR / NXOR) parity structures natively and reduces them into compact algebraic invariants over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} up to 128 variables. 3. Digital Twin Replay (SimulationAgent): Before a synthesized rule is applied, satguardian-advisor.py replays the candidate bitmask against the benign requests stored in waf_ledger.db and reports collisions. The gate is only as good as the recorded benign traffic; it does not establish a fixed false-positive rate. 4. Atomic Hot-Reload (ArcSwap): Validated rules are compiled via compile_equation_to_clauses and hot-swapped into the running Rust Edge WAF via lock-free pointer replacement (ArcSwap) without dropping active TCP connections.

docs.title: SATGuardian Edge WAF — System Architecture & Implementation Reference
docs.text:
Repository: satguardian Version: v0.3.0 Scope: Implementation architecture (Rust hot path & Python control plane)

Status: research prototype, not a production-ready WAF. Metrics in this document are in-sample measurements on a hand-written corpus. The Python comparison harness runs local stand-ins, not real vendor products. See STATUS.md and corpus/README.md.

docs.title: 1. Architectural Overview
docs.text:
satguardian is a hybrid Web Application Firewall (WAF) divided into two strictly decoupled execution planes:

  1. In-Path Edge Data Plane (Native Rust — src/): Evaluates HTTP requests in memory (tens of microseconds per payload; no network hop included) using multi-pass lexical normalization, a 128-bit feature bitmask (FeatureVector(pub u128)), and bitwise rule comparisons ((minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits).
  2. Out-of-Band Control & GXOR Synthesis Plane (Rust & Python — src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, exactor-core-v128, satguardian-advisor.py): Asynchronously reads the SQLite forensic audit ledger (waf_ledger.db), simplifies up to 128 Boolean variables (u128 minterms) using the EXACTOR GXOR engine over the complete {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} operator basis via Differential Gray Code Mapping, validates candidate rules against historical benign traffic in a Digital Twin, and hot-reloads validated rules into the Edge WAF via ArcSwap.

docs.title: Comparative Architecture Notes: SATGuardian and Local Stand-Ins
docs.text:
Subject: how SATGuardian differs from signature, anomaly-scoring, semantic and probabilistic WAF designs, and what the repository actually measures Target system: satguardian v0.3.0

Status: research prototype. This is not a vendor benchmark. The Python harness runs local reimplementations of each technique, not Coraza, SafeLine, ModSecurity or a trained NLP model. Detection numbers are in-sample on a hand-written corpus. See STATUS.md and corpus/README.md.

docs.title: 1. What is being compared
docs.text:
1. SATGuardian: multi-pass lexical normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs), a 128-bit feature bitmask (FeatureVector), and bitwise rule evaluation in src/engine/sat_solver.rs, plus out-of-band EXACTOR GXOR minimization over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} up to 128 variables.
  2. CRS-style stand-in (not Coraza): a few hand-written regex rules with a simple anomaly score over decoded request targets. It does not model the real CRS rule count, paranoia levels or exclusions.
  3. Semantic-token stand-in (not SafeLine): single-pass decode plus a small pattern list. It is not Chaitin's engine.
  4. Probabilistic token stand-in (not a trained model): fixed keyword weights and Shannon entropy. It is not a trained classifier.
  5. Unnormalized regex stand-in (not ModSecurity): deliberately naive signatures over raw fields.

The point of the harness is to regression-test the Python reference port and to illustrate design trade-offs. It cannot rank real products.

docs.title: 3.1 Anomaly scoring
docs.text: Anomaly scoring transforms several request targets and evaluates many rules. That buys coverage and configurability at a per-request CPU cost. The local stand-in implements only a small approximation (20 regex rules), so its latency is not a measurement of real CRS cost. SATGuardian instead normalizes once and evaluates bitmasks; whether that trade-off holds against a real deployment is untested.

docs.title: 3.2 Semantic tokenization
docs.text: Single-pass decoding plus token patterns is cheap, but it can miss nested encodings. The stand-in misses 11.2% of the in-repo attacks, largely on double-encoded traversal. SATGuardian decodes multiple layers; on the pinned corpus it catches those cases after the 2026-11-01 fixes. The corpus was used to drive those fixes, so this is not held-out evidence.

docs.title: 3.3 Probabilistic token scoring
docs.text: Fixed token weights misfire on benign technical prose. The local heuristic blocks 24.6% of the benign controls in the in-repo stream. SATGuardian requires structural conjunctions, and produced no false positives on the 16 benign corpus controls. Sixteen controls cannot support a general false-positive claim.

docs.title: 3.4 Unnormalized regex
docs.text: Raw signature scanning is the cheapest row in the harness and the leakiest on obfuscated payloads (47.0% FNR in this stream). This illustrates why normalization matters; it does not measure ModSecurity.

docs.title: Kubernetes & Envoy Proxy Integration Guide (Native Sidecar Pattern)
docs.text:
Deployment Architecture: On-premise edge inspection (lab configuration) Codebase Reference: src/proxy/envoy_grpc.rs, k8s/envoy-sidecar-deployment.yaml

Status: research prototype. This guide describes an integration that has been exercised in a lab, not a production rollout. See STATUS.md.

docs.title: 1. Overview: Sub-Millisecond Sidecar Inspection
docs.text:
For high-throughput Kubernetes microservices and service meshes (Istio / Envoy), SATGuardian Edge WAF deploys as a lightweight, 100% self-contained native Rust sidecar container alongside each Envoy proxy pod.

Envoy delegates incoming HTTP request authorization to the local SATGuardian daemon via the ext_authz filter over an in-memory Unix Domain Socket (unix:///run/satguardian/waf.sock) or loopback gRPC/HTTP socket, avoiding external network hops.

                      ┌─────────────────────────── Kubernetes Pod ───────────────────────────┐
                      │                                                                      │
Incoming Traffic ────►│  [ Envoy Proxy ] ──(ext_authz UDS)──► [ SATGuardian Rust Sidecar ]   │
  (Ingress/Mesh)      │         │                               (~20 µs avg in-memory eval)  │
                      │         │ (HTTP 200 OK / Allow)                     │                │
                      │         ▼                                           ▼                │
                      │  [ Upstream App Container ]              [ Local waf_ledger.db ]     │
                      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Why the Native Rust Sidecar Pattern Excels
docs.text:
1. Microsecond-Scale Engine Evaluation: satguardian-waf benchmark -r 10000 measures in-memory lexical and bitmask evaluation at roughly 20 µs p50 and 22 µs mean, with p99 fluctuating around 50 µs depending on load. These numbers exclude the UDS hop, Envoy itself and the upstream service; end-to-end sidecar latency has not been characterized.
  2. 100% Traffic Sovereignty & Zero Per-Request Cost: All HTTP payloads stay strictly inside your Kubernetes cluster. There is zero external DNS CNAME routing, zero third-party traffic inspection, and $0.00 cost per request.
  3. Lock-Free Atomic Rule Updates (ArcSwap): When the offline advisor or SATGuardian Cloud synthesizes a minimized u128 rule matrix (consuming Security Units, SU), the sidecar hot-reloads the compiled bitmasks in memory via ArcSwap without restarting pods or dropping connections.
  4. Fail-Safe Continuity: If the organization's monthly Security Units (SU) balance is exhausted (HTTP 402 SU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED), cloud rule synthesis pauses while every Kubernetes sidecar continues inspecting and blocking attacks indefinitely using its last compiled rule matrix.

docs.title: 2. Envoy ext_authz Configuration (envoy.yaml)
docs.text:
Configure Envoy's envoy.filters.http.ext_authz filter to forward request headers and bounded body payloads to the local SATGuardian sidecar:

http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.ext_authz
    typed_config:
      "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ext_authz.v3.ExtAuthz
      transport_api_version: V3
      with_request_body:
        max_request_bytes: 8192
        allow_partial_message: true
        pack_as_bytes: true
      failure_mode_allow: false
      grpc_service:
        envoy_grpc:
          cluster_name: satguardian_ext_authz_cluster
        timeout: 0.05s

clusters:
  - name: satguardian_ext_authz_cluster
    type: STATIC
    connect_timeout: 0.01s
    typed_extension_protocol_options:
      envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions:
        "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions
        explicit_http_config:
          http2_protocol_options: {}
    load_assignment:
      cluster_name: satguardian_ext_authz_cluster
      endpoints:
        - lb_endpoints:
            - endpoint:
                address:
                  pipe:
                    path: /run/satguardian/waf.sock

docs.title: 3. Kubernetes Deployment Manifest (k8s/envoy-sidecar-deployment.yaml)
docs.text:
Mount an in-memory emptyDir (medium: Memory) at /run/satguardian so Envoy and the satguardian-waf sidecar communicate over a shared RAM-backed Unix Domain Socket:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-api-protected
  labels:
    app: payment-api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payment-api
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: satguardian-uds
          emptyDir:
            medium: Memory
      containers:
        - name: satguardian-waf-sidecar
          image: ghcr.io/satguardian/satguardian-waf:v0.2.0
          args:
            - "proxy"
            - "--uds"
            - "/run/satguardian/waf.sock"
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "64Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "128Mi"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: satguardian-uds
              mountPath: /run/satguardian

        - name: envoy-front-proxy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:v1.29-latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts:
            - name: satguardian-uds
              mountPath: /run/satguardian

docs.title: 📋 Configuration File Location
docs.text:
By default, SATGuardian looks for waf_config.toml in the current working directory. You can specify a custom configuration file path using the --config flag or the SATGUARDIAN_CONFIG environment variable:

# Using CLI flag
./satguardian-waf proxy --config /etc/satguardian/waf_config.toml

# Using environment variable
export SATGUARDIAN_CONFIG="/etc/satguardian/waf_config.toml"
./satguardian-waf proxy

docs.title: 🌐 1. Network & Core Defense Settings
docs.text:
Configures the inbound proxy listener, the target upstream application backend, and the active defense mode.

# Inbound HTTP listener address where SATGuardian intercepts incoming web traffic
listen_addr = "0.0.0.0:8080"

# Target upstream backend application (Nginx, Node.js, Python, Go, Java, PHP, IIS, etc.)
upstream_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3000"

# Active perimeter defense mode:
#   "block"   - Active Defense: Instantly drops attacks with HTTP 403 Forbidden.
#   "monitor" - Passive/Dry-Run Mode: Logs attack violations to the ledger but passes traffic upstream.
mode = "block"

docs.text:
Prevents attackers from identifying your security stack through diagnostic response signatures.

# Enable clean web-standard responses
# true  -> Returns clean HTTP 403 Forbidden without leaking rules, proofs, or server signatures.
# false -> Returns diagnostic JSON payloads containing formal causal proofs (useful for debugging).
stealth_mode = true

# (Optional) Custom HTML or plain text body returned during blocked requests when stealth_mode = true
stealth_block_body = "<html><head><title>403 Forbidden</title></head><body><center><h1>403 Forbidden</h1><p>Access Denied by Security Policy</p></center></body></html>"

docs.text:
Manages asynchronous boolean rule synthesis via satguardian.tech and local forensic audit logging.

# SATGuardian Cloud Optimization API URL for EXACTOR GXOR boolean rule minimization
satguardian_api_url = "https://satguardian.tech/api/simplify"

# Cloud API Key (or configure via SATGUARDIAN_API_KEY environment variable)
satguardian_api_key = "ek_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"

# Autonomous background minimization sync interval in seconds (default: 300s / 5 minutes)
autonomous_sync_interval_secs = 300

# Enable automatic hot-reload minimization sync with satguardian.tech
auto_sync_enabled = true

Quota behavior: If your monthly Security Units (SU) quota is exhausted (HTTP 402 SU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED), cloud synthesis pauses and the local Edge WAF keeps serving traffic with its last compiled rule matrix ($0.00 traffic cost).

docs.title: 🛡️ 4. Layer-7 Behavioral Defense & Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Protects against credential stuffing, brute force login floods, and Layer-7 HTTP DDoS attacks using sliding window ring buffers.

# Enable stateful temporal ring buffer analysis
stateful_enabled = true

# Maximum total requests permitted per client IP across all endpoints within the sliding window
stateful_global_limit = 300

# Maximum permitted requests per client IP on sensitive authentication routes (/login, /auth, etc.)
stateful_auth_limit = 20

# Temporal sliding window duration in seconds (60s ring buffer)
stateful_window_secs = 60

# Isolation / jail quarantine duration in seconds for offending IPs (180s = 3 minutes)
stateful_ban_secs = 180

# (Optional) Redis URL for distributed multi-node cluster rate limiting
# redis_url = "redis://127.0.0.1:6379"

docs.text:
Enable or disable pre-compiled domain-specific exploit shields.

[islands]
# WordPress Reconnaissance & Exploit Shield:
# Drops scanner probes targeting /wp-admin, /wp-login.php, xmlrpc.php, and plugin exploits.
# Set to false ONLY if your application legitimately runs WordPress.
wordpress_shield = true

# Sensitive Files & Backdoors Shield:

exposure_shield = true

# Modern Framework Exploits Shield:

framework_shield = true

docs.title: 🎯 7. Customer Business Access Rules ([business_rules])
docs.text:
Declarative access control policies for specific route prefixes, HTTP methods, IP whitelists, blacklists, and mandatory headers.

[business_rules]
enabled = true

# Example 1: Enforce Strict HTTP Method Whitelist on API endpoints
[[business_rules.rules]]
id = "biz-api-methods"
name = "Strict API Method Whitelist"
path_prefix = "/api/v1/"
allowed_methods = ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"]
blocked_methods = ["TRACE", "CONNECT", "PATCH"]
allowed_ips = []
blocked_ips = []
required_headers = []
max_body_bytes = 10485760 # 10 MB payload ceiling
enabled = true

# Example 2: IP-Restricted Internal Administrative Gateway
[[business_rules.rules]]
id = "biz-admin-gateway"
name = "Admin Portal IP Restricted Access"
path_prefix = "/internal/admin/"
allowed_methods = ["GET", "POST"]
blocked_methods = []
allowed_ips = ["127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.1", "192.168.1.100"] # Authorized admin IPs
blocked_ips = []
required_headers = ["X-Admin-Token"] # Mandatory administrative header
max_body_bytes = 1048576 # 1 MB body ceiling
enabled = true

docs.title: Parameter Reference for Business Rules:
docs.text: Parameter Type Description id String Unique rule identifier. name String Human-readable description of the rule. path_prefix String URL path prefix target (e.g. /api/, /admin/). allowed_methods Array Allowed HTTP methods (e.g. ["GET", "POST"]). blocked_methods Array Blocked HTTP methods (e.g. ["TRACE", "PATCH"]). allowed_ips Array Client IP whitelist (if non-empty, unlisted IPs are blocked). blocked_ips Array Client IP blacklist (listed IPs are instantly dropped). required_headers Array Mandatory HTTP headers required for request approval. max_body_bytes Integer Maximum permitted HTTP body size in bytes. enabled Boolean true to activate rule, false to disable.

docs.title: Technical Audit & Empirical Verification Report: satguardian (SATGuardian Edge WAF)
docs.text:
Audit Scope: Code review of src/ (Rust), satguardian_waf/ (Python) and the bundled SQLite ledger Target Version: v0.3.0 Audit Objective: Check implementation claims against source, and report only measurements that can be reproduced from the repository.

Status: research prototype, not a production-ready WAF. Earlier revisions of this report capped accuracy at 99.9%, floored error rates at < 0.1%, and labelled Python stand-ins as vendor products. Those claims were fabricated or misleading and have been removed. See STATUS.md.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary: What Is Implemented vs. Theoretical Research
docs.text:
A line-by-line review of the satguardian repository and adjacent workspace projects (hesize-code-ia, adn, guardian-api-, optimizador_bayesiano, f32) distinguishes implemented code from external research concepts:

Technical Concept Status in satguardian Actual Code Implementation & Location Multi-Pass Lexical Normalization & Tokenization ✅ Implemented src/ast/lexer.rs (Lexer::normalize_and_tokenize) and satguardian_waf/core/solver_sat.py unwind nested URL/HTML encodings, strip /*...*/ comments, and extract structural tokens across 5 attack domains (SQLi, XSS, RCE, LFI, SSRF). 128-Bit Feature Vector (u128) ✅ Implemented src/ast/features.rs (FeatureVector(pub u128)) packs HTTP metadata, Shannon entropy flags, and lexical token presence into a 128-bit integer. Bitmask Conjunction Evaluator ("SAT Engine") ✅ Implemented src/engine/sat_solver.rs (SatEngine) evaluates pre-compiled boolean cubes in \(O(1)\) per rule via bitwise AND: (minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits. (Note: It is a fast bitmask evaluator, not an in-path backtracking DPLL/CDCL SAT solver). Out-of-Band EXACTOR GXOR Minimization ✅ Implemented src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs (SatguardianCloudClient::simplify) and exactor-core-v128 (procesar_gxor, modify_gray_code) simplify up to 128 Boolean variables (u128 minterms) out of band using the {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} operator basis and Differential Gray Code Mapping in \(O(\text{term\_count})\) linear time. Digital Twin Benign Traffic Replay ✅ Implemented satguardian-advisor.py (SimulationAgent) replays candidate rules against benign requests recorded in waf_ledger.db and reports collisions. It does not certify a fixed false-positive rate. Lock-Free Atomic Rule Hot-Reload ✅ Implemented src/proxy/http_proxy.rs uses arc_swap::ArcSwap to swap rule matrices in memory without dropping TCP connections. Token-Bucket Burst Rate Limiting ✅ Implemented src/engine/sat_solver.rs uses lock-free DashMap counters per client IP to block Layer-7 burst floods (SAT-STATE-01). Wolfram Cellular Automata / M-Code / Graph Isomorphism ❌ Not in WAF Code Part of separate theoretical research projects (hesize-code-ia, adn); removed from all WAF documentation to maintain strict engineering accuracy.

docs.text:

The ledger is demo data for exercising the advisor pipeline, not independently labelled ground truth and not a customer tenant.

docs.title: SATGuardian Edge WAF: Sub-Millisecond Lexical Normalization, 128-Bit Boolean Mask Evaluation, and Out-of-Band EXACTOR GXOR Rule Synthesis
docs.text:
Technical White Paper — Version 3.0 (Research Prototype Edition) Implementation Reference: satguardian (src/ in Rust, satguardian_waf/ in Python) & exactor-core-v128 (EXACTOR GXOR Engine)

Status: research prototype, not a production-ready WAF. Evaluation is in-sample on a small hand-written corpus; competitor rows are local Python stand-ins. See Project Status.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
Modern Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) face a fundamental engineering tension between inspection latency, evasion resistance, and false positive rates. Unnormalized regular expression engines are cheap per request but miss nested encodings and inline comments. Anomaly-scoring rule sets transform several request targets and evaluate many rules. Token-weight classifiers can fire on benign technical prose. Those statements are design-level; this repository does not benchmark the real products, only local Python stand-ins.

This paper presents the implemented architecture and the measurements available for SATGuardian Edge WAF (satguardian). SATGuardian decouples in-path request evaluation from out-of-band boolean rule minimization: 1. In-Path Hot Plane (Native Rust): Applies bounded multi-pass lexical normalization (src/ast/lexer.rs), packs structural tokens and request attributes into a 128-bit integer (FeatureVector(pub u128) in src/ast/features.rs), and evaluates compiled rule cubes via bitwise operations ((minterm & required_mask) == expected_bits in src/engine/sat_solver.rs). On the pinned corpus at 10,000 requests, a representative run measured p50 ~20 µs, mean ~22 µs, and p99 near 50 µs, single-threaded, in memory only. 2. Out-of-Band Synthesis Plane (Rust & Python): Logs novel anomalous u128 minterms to a local SQLite ledger (waf_ledger.db), simplifies up to 128 Boolean variables asynchronously using the EXACTOR GXOR engine over the complete {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} operator basis via Differential Gray Code Mapping, replays candidates against recorded benign traffic to find collisions, and hot-reloads compiled bitmasks via lock-free ArcSwap.

docs.title: 1.1 Lexical Normalization & Feature Vector Mapping
docs.text:
Let an incoming HTTP request be represented by the tuple \(r = (M, P, Q, H, B)\) denoting method, path, query string, headers, and body.

The lexical normalizer \(\mathcal{N}\) (src/ast/lexer.rs) applies bounded iterative percent-decoding (\(k \le 3\) passes) and inline comment stripping (/*...*/) to produce a canonical byte stream \(s = \mathcal{N}(r)\), from which it extracts a set of structural tokens \(\mathcal{T}(s)\) and maps \(r\) into a 128-bit boolean feature vector:

\[\mathbf{v}(r) \in \{0, 1\}^{128} \quad (\text{represented in Rust as } \texttt{u128})\]

Each bit \(v_i \in \{0, 1\}\) (\(i \in \{0, \dots, 127\}\)) encodes a deterministic predicate (e.g., presence of SQL tautology tokens, UNION SELECT projection, executable <script> or inline DOM event attributes, shell command chaining operators, relative path traversal sequences, or high character Shannon entropy \(H(s) > \tau\)).

docs.title: 1.2 In-Path Bitmask Cube Evaluation (src/engine/sat_solver.rs)
docs.text:
Each compiled security rule \(c_j\) is a boolean cube (product term / conjunction of literals) represented by two 128-bit integers: - required_mask (\(M_j \in \texttt{u128}\)): Bitmask indicating which of the 128 variables participate in rule \(j\). - expected_bits (\(E_j \in \texttt{u128}\)): Expected polarity (1 for positive literal, 0 for negated literal) of those active variables.

At runtime, evaluating whether request \(\mathbf{v}(r)\) triggers rule \(c_j\) requires a single bitwise AND and equality check:

\[\text{Match}(\mathbf{v}(r), c_j) \iff (\mathbf{v}(r) \mathbin{\&} M_j) == E_j\]

If no rule cube matches (\(\forall j, \, (\mathbf{v}(r) \mathbin{\&} M_j) \neq E_j\)), the security invariant holds and the request is allowed. Unlike backtracking regular expressions or NP-complete in-path DPLL/CDCL solvers, bitwise evaluation over \(R\) rules executes in deterministic \(O(R)\) CPU cycles.

docs.title: 1.3 Out-of-Band EXACTOR GXOR Minimization (src/cloud/satguardian_client.rs, exactor-core-v128)
docs.text: When unobserved malicious minterms \(\mathcal{M} = \{m_1, m_2, \dots, m_k\} \subset \{0, 1\}^{n}\) (\(n \le 128\)) are collected in waf_ledger.db, classical {AND, OR, NOT} minimizers (such as Quine-McCluskey or Espresso) suffer from \(O(2^n)\) exponential blow-up beyond 20–30 variables. Instead, the out-of-band synthesizer invokes the EXACTOR GXOR engine (procesar_gxor in exactor-core-v128) via SatguardianCloudClient::simplify: 1. Differential Gray Code Mapping (modify_gray_code): Projects 128-bit minterms into a Gray Code space and locates logical neighbors differing by a single bit (\(\text{popcount}(E_a \oplus E_b) = 1\)) in \(O(1)\) constant time via BTreeMap/HashMap lookups, achieving \(O(\text{term\_count})\) linear complexity: $\(M_{\text{merged}} = M_a \mathbin{\&} \neg(E_a \oplus E_b), \quad E_{\text{merged}} = E_a \mathbin{\&} M_{\text{merged}}\)$ 2. GXOR / NXOR Algebraic Reduction over {AND, OR, NOT, XOR}: Detects exclusive-OR (\(\oplus\)) and equivalence (\(\odot\)) structures across up to 128 Boolean variables (u128), collapsing parity and symmetric attack predicates that would otherwise require exponentially many Sum-of-Products (SOP) clauses. 3. Digital Twin Collision Replay (satguardian-advisor.py): Before a reduced invariant \(c^*\) is added to the active rule matrix, the SimulationAgent replays it against the benign records stored in waf_ledger.db and reports any collision. The ledger in this repository is demo data, so the replay finds collisions; it does not certify a fixed false-positive rate.

docs.title: 2. Evaluation: What Was Measured, and What Was Not
docs.text: No vendor comparison has been run. The Python harness in this repository contains local stand-ins for a CRS-style anomaly scorer, a semantic ruleset and a token-weight classifier. They are Python reimplementations written here, not Coraza, SafeLine, ModSecurity or any commercial product. Their numbers describe this repository's stand-ins only.

docs.title: 2.1 Detection on the Pinned Corpus
docs.text:
corpus/independent_v1.json holds 63 labelled attacks and 16 benign controls; corpus/heldout_v1.json holds 17 attack variants and 4 benign controls. The first run of each file was recorded before any fix and is the only number in this repository that was not produced by tuning against the same data.

Corpus First run (before fixes) Current regression run Interpretation independent_v1 51/63 attacks (80.95%), 3/16 benign blocked (18.75%) 63/63 attacks, 0/16 benign blocked In-sample regression after fixes heldout_v1 11/17 attacks (64.71%), 0/4 benign blocked (0.00%) 17/17 attacks, 0/4 benign blocked Batch consumed by the fix pass; in-sample now

The first-run row is the honest statement about the engine as originally published: it missed roughly one attack in five and blocked three benign requests. The current row says the pinned cases pass. It is not a held-out estimate and it is not evidence of production accuracy. Rules for adding cases and the full miss list live in Detection Corpus.

docs.title: 2.2 In-Memory Latency (Native Rust)
docs.text: satguardian-waf benchmark -r 10000 cycles the corpus and measures rule evaluation only. A representative run on the development machine reported p50 near 20 µs, mean near 22 µs and p99 near 50 µs, single-threaded. The figures move with machine load and should be re-measured on the target host. Excluded from the measurement: network, TLS, reverse-proxy hops, upstream calls, and SQLite ledger writes. The runner prints these exclusions and the in-sample caveat on every run, and it refuses to start if the corpus file is missing.

docs.title: 2.3 Python Reference Harness (Local Stand-Ins)
docs.text:
python run_benchmark.py 1000 runs the Python reference port of the engine against the local stand-ins on the in-repo payload list. Every row is labelled with its provenance in the report output, the Markdown export and the API response. Representative 1,000-request values:

Engine Implementation Attacks detected Benign blocked Mean latency SATGuardian Python reference Python port (not the Rust engine) 100.0% 0.0% ~0.06 ms CRS-style anomaly stand-in Python reimplementation 97.3% 0.0% ~0.24 ms Semantic-ruleset stand-in Python reimplementation 94.4% 0.0% ~0.06 ms Token-weight stand-in Python heuristic 77.3% 24.6% ~0.07 ms Unnormalized regex stand-in Python reimplementation 76.5% 0.0% ~0.04 ms

Both the payload list and the stand-ins were written in this repository, so these are in-sample results over a small hand-written set. They show that the harness runs end to end. They do not support any claim about real products, and they do not establish production readiness.

docs.title: 2.4 Engineering Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Normalization drives the detection gap. The first-run misses were concentrated in MySQL executable comments, || tautologies, HTML-entity schemes, overlong UTF-8, \u-escaped keys and nested Log4Shell lookups. The fixes were lexical: additional decoding passes and normalization rules, not a larger rule table.
  2. Structural conjunctions avoid keyword false positives in the pinned set. The three first-run false positives were a <script src> include, a data: URI and a localhost URL in prose. Requiring co-occurring structural tokens removed them without deleting the cases.
  3. Per-request cost is dominated by normalization, not rule matching. The bitmask test is one AND plus one comparison per rule; the decode loop runs first and sets the floor. This ordering is why the in-memory figure is tens of microseconds rather than single digits.
  4. None of this is an independent evaluation. The corpus is small and hand-written, and it has been used to drive fixes. A defensible quality claim needs a held-out corpus built and labelled by someone who has not seen the engine, plus a production soak. Neither exists yet. See Project Status.

docs.title: 3. Sovereign Deployment & Security Units (SU) Licensing Model
docs.text: SATGuardian is designed for 100% on-premise data sovereignty: - Zero Traffic Hosting: Customer DNS CNAMEs never point to SATGuardian servers. The Edge WAF deploys as a Standalone Rust Binary, a Reverse Proxy in front of Nginx/Apache/IIS, or a Kubernetes Envoy Sidecar (unix:///run/satguardian/waf.sock). - 100% Free & Unlimited Edge Inspection: In-path traffic inspection carries zero per-request fees ($0.00 / 1M requests). - Cloud Optimization via Security Units (SU): Only out-of-band cloud boolean minimization (EXACTOR GXOR {AND, OR, NOT, XOR} synthesis up to 128 variables) consumes Security Units (SU) across five tiers (Scout $20/mo up to 20 vars, Pro/Dev $49/mo up to 64 vars, Startup $499/mo up to 128 vars, Scale $2,499/mo up to 128 vars, and Enterprise custom up to 128 variables; 256+ variables are delivered as dedicated bare-metal Engineering Expansion Projects). When a plan's monthly SU quota is exhausted (HTTP 402 SU_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED), cloud optimization pauses while the Edge WAF continues serving traffic with its last compiled bitmask matrix.
